description: A word is a motif. Each episode is a master's thesis on that word — its history, philosophy, science, and the stories it carries. The word is the door; the journey is the content.

structure.principle: Interesting enough to choose; forgiving enough to drift away from

section_1.title: The Word Today
section_1.purpose: Ground the listener in the modern meaning
section_1.content: Definition. Common usage. How we encounter it daily.
section_1.example: Vegetable. A plant grown for its edible parts. We eat them every day. But the word is older than cooking. Older than farming. Older than agriculture itself.

section_2.title: The Etymology
section_2.content: Root language. Proto-forms. How it traveled. What it originally meant.
section_2.example: From Latin 'vegetabilis' — able to grow. From 'vegetare' — to enliven. From 'vegetus' — lively, vigorous. The word originally meant 'alive' — not 'edible'.

section_3.title: The Historical Journey
section_3.purpose: How the word traveled through time
section_3.content: Century by century. Who used it. How meaning shifted. The social context.
section_3.example: In the 14th century, 'vegetable' meant any living plant. By the 16th century, it meant plants grown for food. The word narrowed as agriculture specialized.

section_4.title: The Philosophy
section_4.purpose: What the word reveals about how we think
section_4.content: Aristotle's classification. The boundary between alive and not-alive. What we include and exclude. The ethics of naming.
section_4.example: Aristotle classified all living things. Plants were 'vegetative' — they grew but didn't move. Animals were 'sensitive' — they moved and felt. Humans were 'rational' — we thought. The word 'vegetable' carries this ancient taxonomy in its bones.

section_5.title: The Science
section_5.purpose: What we know now that they didn't
section_5.content: Modern understanding. Photosynthesis. Cell biology. The microbiome. How science reshaped the word.
section_5.example: We now know plants feel. They respond to touch, light, gravity. The 'vegetative' state isn't passive — it's a different kind of intelligence. Aristotle was wrong. The word remembers his mistake.

section_6.title: The Return
section_6.purpose: Circle back to the word with new understanding
section_6.content: What the word means now. How the journey changed it. The comfort of understanding.
section_6.example: Vegetable. A word that carried Aristotle's philosophy, medieval agriculture, modern science, and your dinner plate. Every time you say it, you're speaking 2,000 years of human thought. Sleep well.

branching_rules.the_word_today: Always start here. Ground the listener.
branching_rules.the_etymology: Always include. This is the anchor.
branching_rules.the_history: Branch into relevant historical periods. Each century gets a paragraph.
branching_rules.the_philosophy: Branch into relevant philosophers, thinkers, ideas. This is the meat.
branching_rules.the_science: Branch into modern understanding. Contrast with ancient views.
branching_rules.the_return: Always end here. Circle back. The comfort of understanding.

nice_to_have: Counterintuitive meaning (word means something different now)
avoid: Words that are too modern (no historical journey)
